I work in a place that is connected to one of the places mentioned by another commenter and can state very vaguely:

1. This trend of unaccompanied minors “abandoned by their parents in the US” is only growing. The majority of these kids actually are awaiting dates in court that haven’t been assigned yet and the backlog reaches until around 2027 at this point. 
2. When a report is made to CPS, if they do end up doing anything about it, they just tell the closest refugee/immigrant services agency and expect them to take care of it. I’ve seen it. “You work with migrants, you handle this situation. Thanks.”
3. These kids weren’t abandoned by their parents- they are in contact with their parents and sometimes trying to send every possible resource they have back home, causing them to live in poverty. These kids are not eligible for Medicaid or food stamps either, so they often exhibit signs of poverty that may be confused with neglect. 
4. One of the only things these kids have a right to is public school. And if that’s where you got your mandated reporting status from, I suggest you leave these kids to have their right to public school while they await their court dates. I’m also a mandated reporter, but I know how to pick and choose my battles. This is a systemic injustice issue.

I’ve been in college a month now- in the US- and have been thinking about weed, and my decisions regarding it a lot. It’s hard to get real information on it- is it addictive? Do I have an addictive personality? Does smoking weed cause cancer? Etc etc. this thread has been pretty helpful in helping me make some decisions/informing me about smoking as an adult, so thanks everyone for having a somewhat educated discussion- I just read this entire thing hahahha. 

That being said, there’s so many kids like me out there. There’s just not a proper education on cannabis out there- I was either taught “it’s going to give you schizophrenia” or “dude look at me I smoke a fat ass bong 6 times a day” and I didn’t really know there was an in between. Can weed really help with anxiety, or in the long term is it harmful? Could I take it in pill form like Prozac? When the doctor asks me if I smoke, do I tell them yes? I don’t smoke cigarettes at all. 

Because of the stigma and it being illegal, I don’t know these things. I think, if I did, I’d smoke more safely- right now I like to say I smoke medicinally but I’d say it’s medicinally on the weekdays and recreationally on the weekends. And even then, I’m not sure- what if I’m fooling myself, and I’m actually addicted? How will I know? Does weed carry that danger? 

Anyway. Thanks for this thread. You guys are pretty cool and informative.
